chunks.label: CRM and Leads
chunks.h: Teams, territories and who can see what
chunks.t: Selling and servicing a large account is rarely one person's job. The record supports the whole team without everyone seeing everything. Account teams: Attach the people who work on an account with a role on that account: who sells it, who services it, who handles the billing, who is the escalation point. Each one is named on the record rather than inferred from who happened to touch it last. Territories and assignment: Define territories by area, postcode or service line and let an account be assigned automatically when it arrives, so a new lead lands with the right person without a manual sorting step. Roles that scope access: A role is a set of permissions. Scoped to a territory or a district, it means a salesperson sees their own patch and a manager sees all of it, and neither has to be maintained by hand. Sharing on the account: An account can be shared with specific people or a who

chunks.label: CRM and Leads
chunks.h: Who sold it, and who gets paid for it
chunks.t: Three different people can be responsible for one sale, and collapsing them into a single owner column is how commission disputes start. AlphaFlux records three separate roles on an account. Who sold it, which is the person owed commission. Who services it, which is the technician or team who keeps it. And who booked it, which distinguishes a lead that came from a person from one that came from an agent or an import. Splits are recorded in basis points and must total exactly one hundred percent before they can be saved. A split that does not add up is not a rounding problem to be tolerated, it is a commission error waiting to be discovered at the worst moment. Attribution history is append-only. When ownership changes, the previous entry is superseded rather than overwritten, so a payout made in March can still be explained in September, and revenue an agent generated stays separable fro

chunks.label: Inventory
chunks.h: Inventory is included on the free plan, permanently
chunks.t: Most platforms treat stock as an enterprise feature. A one person operation with a van full of parts needs it just as much as a depot does, so it is not gated. Every account gets items, movements, locations and low stock alerts at no cost, whether there is one technician or two hundred. What grows with the plan is scale, not capability: how many locations you can define, how much movement history you keep, and how far the reporting reaches. The point is that the record starts on day one. A company that tracks its stock from the first van never has to reconstruct a year of purchases later, and never has to run an inventory count to find out what it owns. Items and stock levels: Parts, products and consumables with SKU, quantity on hand, reorder point, unit and cost. Locations that match reality: Trucks, vans, storage units, rented bays, depots, yards and branches, each with its own stock

chunks.label: Inventory
chunks.h: Chemical and controlled stock, signed in and out
chunks.t: Some things in a van are not ordinary stock. They are regulated, they have a usage rate, they must be accounted for, and an inspector may ask. AlphaFlux tracks them the way they are actually used. A container is signed in when it is received, assigned to a technician or a location, and signed out when it is used or returned. The record shows who had it, when they took it, where it went and what remains. That record is what turns a difficult conversation into a report. Usage per technician, usage per service, what was applied at a customer's property, and what is currently unaccounted for are all available as views rather than as an afternoon with a clipboard. The same mechanism handles any stock that needs a chain of custody: calibrated instruments, keys, PPE, high value tools, controlled parts, and anything else where knowing that it left the building is not enough. chunks.label: Inventory

chunks.t: The same records serve a sole trader with a van and an operation with units in every time zone. These are the arrangements the module is designed around. Technician and vehicle stock: Every truck holds its own position, so the question where is that part is answered by naming the part rather than by ringing three technicians. A technician's stock moves when the job consumes it, not when someone remembers to update a sheet. Storage units and rented bays: A rented storage locker is a location like any other. It can hold stock, it can be transferred to and from, and it can be counted without an afternoon of driving to it and writing things down. Mobile and self contained units: Self contained units that move between sites, whether that is a mobile workshop, a solar powered field unit, a trailer or a container, are tracked as both an asset and a location. chunks.label: Inventory

chunks.t: A stock system only works if a technician will actually use it from a driveway. Everything here is designed to take seconds. Adjust in two taps: Search or scan, enter the quantity, pick a reason. Add a note if it needs one. Transfer between places: Move stock from depot to truck to site, with a record at each end and an in transit state so nothing is ever in two places. Counts that reconcile: Run a count on one location, see the variance against the system, and post the adjustment with a reason. chunks.t: A phone system that does not connect to the job it produced is a phone system that costs you a re-typing job every day. Numbers you control: Bring the numbers your customers already know, or buy new ones by area code. Each number gets its own behaviour. Texting that belongs to the account: Every inbound and outbound message lands on the customer timeline, not in a separate handset. Call handling per number: Greeting, ring through target, business hours and an after hours rule, configured per number rather than once for the whole company. A receptionist that books: The AI answers first, checks real capacity and puts the job on the schedule. Emergencies go straight to a person. A voicemail inbox that reads: Recordings, playback and transcripts in the console, with an unread count so nothing sits unheard for a week. Missed call text back: A missed call triggers a text within seconds, which

chunks.label: AI Phone Answering
chunks.h: How a call is handled, decision by decision
chunks.t: Every number carries its own rule set. Here is the order the platform works through when the phone rings. Answer: The call is answered immediately, so the caller never hears a ring they can hang up on. Receptionist or person: If the number has an AI receptionist attached, it is dialled first with a fifteen second window. If it does not answer, the human chain runs as if the AI had never been there. If the AI does answer, nobody's phone rings. Inside or outside hours: Business hours are set per number and per day. Inside hours the call rings through to the right person. Outside hours it follows the after hours rule you chose. The after hours rule: Three options per number: take a voicemail, forward to a number such as an answering service, or end the call politely. Which one is right depends on the business, so it is a setting rather than an assumption. Voicemail and text back: When a voi

chunks.label: AI Phone Answering
chunks.h: The receptionist does the parts you would rather not staff
chunks.t: Answering the phone at nine at night is expensive to staff and cheap to automate, as long as it is done properly. It identifies the caller, works out which office serves the address, checks whether the service described is one you offer, and books the visit against real capacity. It takes the details, leaves a complete record, and hands over to a person for anything that needs judgement. It is bounded by the same rules your staff are: the service areas you actually cover, the capacity your technicians actually have, and a list of things it must never do. It does not quote a price that is not on your list, and it does not promise an exact arrival time. The script lives inside AlphaFlux and is versioned, so changing how your business answers the phone is an edit rather than a ticket to a vendor. Right office, first time: The address is resolved against the areas each office covers before a

chunks.label: AI Phone Answering
chunks.t: Business texting has rules. The platform handles the registration and the compliance so messages arrive. Brand and campaign registration: The registration work that carriers require before application to person messaging is supported in the console, with the status of each registration visible rather than hidden. Opt out handling: A customer who replies to stop is suppressed from future sends automatically. That applies equally to a person sending and to an agent sending. Message logging on the account: Every message in and out is recorded against the customer timeline, with the number it came from and the person or agent who sent it. Deliverability signals: Failed and undelivered messages are surfaced rather than silently dropped, because a text that never arrived is worse than one never sent. chunks.h: Question: Do I have to port my numbers?
chunks.t: No, and in most cases you should not. You can connect the carrier account you already have so your existing numbers keep working and stay yours. Porting is only needed if you want the number managed under a different carrier account.

chunks.label: AI Phone Answering
chunks.h: Question: Can the AI receptionist take a payment?
chunks.t: It does not take card details on a call, and that is deliberate. It can book the work, take the details and leave a record, and payment is collected through the normal invoicing route where the customer has a receipt and you have a record.

chunks.label: AI Phone Answering
chunks.h: Question: What happens if the AI does not understand the caller?
chunks.t: It hands over. If it cannot place the call in one of the categories it handles, or if the caller asks for a person, or if it is an emergency, the call moves to a human by the rule you set for that number.

chunks.label: AI Phone Answering

chunks.t: Recordings and transcriptions are available on the plans that include them, attached to the customer account rather than sitting in a separate call list.

chunks.t: Each office can have its own numbers and its own call handling, and the receptionist resolves callers to the correct office by address. A central number can also route by the caller's location.
